description: What the diagnostics of ONE destination show after a scenario (REQ-DGN-001, REQ-DGN-002). One destination; batch_size 10 and a flush interval of 60000 ms, so nothing is sent until the scenario calls Flush once with a generous timeout; events (at most 10) are queued first, so the Flush sends ONE batch of all of them. Backoff base 1 ms and ceiling 5 ms, a random source that always answers 0.5. answers are the SendResult of each call to the destination (when they are used up the last one repeats) and are consistent: accepted + dropped + failed is events. Rules of the batch are those of mode_scenarios.json. Counters: attempts (calls), retries (calls beyond the first), batches (always 1), delivered (the accepted events of the answer that ends the batch), dropped (events lost: dropped by the destination, or failed until retry_limit_reached), failed_events (events a best_effort answer failed), export_failures (calls in which the answer had failed or dropped events), serialization_failures and configuration_errors (the failed plus dropped events of EACH answer whose reason is serialization_failed or configuration_error), last_batch_size and max_batch_size (the events of the batch), dropped_by_reason (an empty reason counts as unspecified). has_last_success is true when the destination accepted at least one event. last_flush is the result of the Flush for this destination (sent = delivered, dropped = events - delivered, spooled 0). diagnostics is the list of the diagnostics the channel publishes, in order, with the rate limit set high enough to suppress none: an answer with failed events gives export_failed (the reason, unspecified when empty, and the failed count) at EACH call; the answer that ends the batch gives, for its dropped events, the code of the reason (serialization_failed, configuration_error or events_dropped) with its dropped count, or events_dropped with the reason retry_limit_reached and the failed count when the batch ran out of attempts. The latency of the calls and the times are not part of this file.

cases.name: best_effort_all_accepted
cases.description: Nothing goes wrong: every counter of a failure stays at zero.

cases.name: best_effort_transient_failure_is_not_retried
cases.description: A failing answer is one export failure, the events count as failed and one diagnostic says so.

cases.name: best_effort_failure_without_reason
cases.description: A failure without a reason is reported as unspecified.

cases.name: best_effort_partial
cases.description: Two events taken and one failed.

cases.name: best_effort_permanent_rejection
cases.description: Dropped events are counted under the reason of the answer and reported once.

cases.name: best_effort_serialization_failed
cases.description: The reason serialization_failed is also counted as a serialization failure and has its own code.

cases.name: best_effort_configuration_error
cases.description: The reason configuration_error is counted as a configuration error and has its own code.

cases.name: best_effort_dropped_without_reason
cases.description: A drop without a reason is counted under unspecified.

cases.name: best_effort_failed_and_dropped
cases.description: One answer with failed and dropped events gives two diagnostics, the failure first.

cases.name: retry_recovers
cases.description: Two transient failures and a success: three attempts, two retries, two export failures and delivered once.

cases.name: retry_limit_reached
cases.description: Every attempt fails: the events are dropped under retry_limit_reached after the last attempt.

cases.name: retry_permanent_rejection_is_not_retried
cases.description: A permanent rejection ends the batch at once.

cases.name: retry_partial_failure_resends_whole_batch
cases.description: A partial failure sends the whole batch again; only the last answer decides what was delivered.

cases.name: retry_limit_with_partial_acceptance
cases.description: At the limit the accepted events of the last answer are delivered and the failed ones are dropped.
